correctness.rationale: The open-neighborhood fold is a contiguous retraction: whenever a face contains the source vertex, it can also contain the target. An independent reconstruction applies this from the tips, simultaneously sending depth L−2 to depth L on every arm for L≥3. The requisite containment of neighborhoods follows because the tip has just the neighbor at depth L−1; all replacements are compatible across arms. For L≥4 the remaining graph is the spider with length L−3 plus m disjoint two-vertex paths, so on independence realizations the recurrence is an equivariant join with S(V_m). For L=3 the center is isolated after the fold, so the complex is an invariant cone. For L=2, the link of the center is the simplex on the tips: replace the center by its invariant barycenter linearly on the cone, fixing the center-deletion complex, which is the join of the m two-point path complexes. For L=1 the center and the leaf simplex give a trivial two-point model. Iterating and using the weight-square-root homeomorphism from a join of unit spheres to the unit sphere of their direct sum verifies all three formulas and their equivariance. Actual H-fixed points have constant barycentric coordinate on each vertex orbit. Such an orbit is independent (all vertices at one depth on distinct arms), and two allowed orbits are incompatible exactly when their corresponding vertices are adjacent in the smaller spider. Summing orbit coordinates and dividing by orbit size on the inverse are affine on the relevant cells and give the asserted PL homeomorphism. The fixed subspace of V_m has one coordinate per arm orbit and its determinant on a permutation is the sign, which gives all dimensions and orientation characters, including trivial S^0 at L=1. The submitted finite checker was inspected, not run: its trace tests compare cyclic fixed-space Euler characteristics, not PL homeomorphisms or all subgroup models. The PL and integral assertions are checked by the proof, not by that marker.

originality.rationale: Earlier sources cover the ordinary path and spider homotopy types and supply generic folding techniques. The supported distinct claim on the record's publication chronology is the actual simultaneous arm-permutation equivariant model and geometric fixed-space description, not the ordinary residue table. The separate November 22 Resultary theorem mathematically duplicates the substantive equivariant, fixed-space and character conclusions on the common domain (m≥3, L≥2) and adds two-arm quotient results; it is later than the assigned November 1 catalogue publication. The November 17 fixed-forest theorem also gives later, broader coverage of the fixed-space component. Neither later date is evidence of earlier publication, and neither comparison establishes independence or priority beyond the inspected publication record. The L=1 base case is elementary and is not the basis for the originality pass.
residual_risks: An earlier unindexed treatment of equivariant tree folds or a prior version of the later matching theorem could affect priority. The inspected later records establish mathematical coverage, not who obtained the result independently or first.
